description: Milestone 2: live dashboard. Add the signal processing pipeline (amplitude decoding already exists in backend/csi_parser.py; add normalization, outlier filtering, smoothing, motion activity score, baseline deviation, data-quality assessment) and a background acquisition engine, then a dark-mode Streamlit dashboard showing connection status, packet rate, signal quality, a scrolling subcarrier heatmap, amplitude over time, motion activity and baseline deviation in real time from a serial port or a replay file. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Create backend/config.py: dataclasses with JSON load/save for ProcessingConfig (window_s=1.0, hampel window/threshold, ema_alpha, min_packet_rate_hz=20, min_window_fill=0.7, use_lltf_valid_subcarriers=True), MotionThresholds (low/movement/rapid score thresholds with sensible uncalibrated defaults), and an AppConfig aggregating them, stored at data/config.json (created with defaults if missing).

Create backend/processing.py: streaming SignalProcessor that consumes CSIPacket objects and maintains per-packet feature history. Steps per packet: take LLTF amplitudes at VALID_LLTF_INDICES (respect first_word_invalid masking), normalize by per-packet mean amplitude (reduces AGC/gain jumps; keep raw too), Hampel-style outlier rejection per subcarrier over a short history, EMA (or scipy lfilter low-pass) smoothing. Over a sliding window (window_s, using host timestamps) compute: mean per-subcarrier std of normalized amplitude (variance feature), first-difference energy (temporal feature), baseline deviation (mean |profile - baseline_mean| / baseline_std when a baseline is available, else deviation from a slow EMA reference), and a combined motion_score that is normalized by the calibrated noise level when calibration exists (empty room ~1.0). Expose MotionFrame dataclass (ts, motion_score, variance, diff_energy, baseline_deviation, rssi, packet_rate, quality ok/reasons). Data-quality: insufficient if packet rate < min_packet_rate_hz, window fill < min_window_fill, CSI length changed mid-window, or stale data (>1 s since last packet); report reasons. Handle variable CSI len gracefully (reset history on layout change).

Create backend/activity.py with classify_activity(frame, thresholds) -> one of 'unknown' (insufficient data quality), 'empty_low' (Empty room / low activity), 'movement', 'rapid_movement'; the 'potential_fall' state is added by the detector in FEAT-004, so design the enum/labels to include it now (display names: 'Empty room / low activity', 'Movement detected', 'Rapid movement', 'Potential fall', 'Unknown / insufficient data').

Create backend/engine.py: Engine owning a LineSource (SerialSource, ReplaySource; simulation source plugs in later), the parser, PacketBuffer, SignalProcessor and a bounded deque of MotionFrames (e.g. last 120 s), running in a daemon thread with start()/stop()/switch_source(). Thread-safe snapshot() returning copies for UI: connection status, source kind ('live'|'replay'|'simulation') and a synthetic flag, configuration info (chip family, channel, bandwidth, secondary channel, CSI len, TX MAC seen, last EG_RX_STATS), packet counters and rates, RSSI stats, recent amplitude matrix (N packets x 52 subcarriers) for the heatmap, mean amplitude series, motion frames, current activity class. Never synthesize values: empty snapshot fields when no data.

Create dashboard/app.py (Streamlit) and .streamlit/config.toml (dark theme base='dark' with a modern accent color, server.headless default false, browser.gatherUsageStats=false, no external assets). Hold the Engine in st.cache_resource; sidebar to choose source: Live serial (port dropdown from backend.ports with auto option, baud, connect/disconnect), Replay file (pick from data/recordings and tests/fixtures, speed, loop). Main view uses st.fragment(run_every=~0.5 s) to refresh: A) status cards: TX/RX configuration (channel, bandwidth, TX MAC, chip family, CSI len), serial connection status/reconnects, packet rate, RSSI, noise floor, malformed/seq gaps, signal quality badge with reasons; B) plotly charts: scrolling subcarrier amplitude heatmap (time x subcarrier), mean amplitude over time, motion activity score with threshold lines, baseline deviation; C) current activity class badge (colored). Persistent caption: 'Research prototype. Not a medical device. Predictions are not medically validated.' Show a prominent banner whenever source is replay (and later simulation) so users never confuse it with live data.
Update Makefile `dashboard` target to `.venv/bin/streamlit run dashboard/app.py` (the one-command start) and add `run_dashboard.sh` wrapper that creates the venv if missing.

Add tests: tests/test_processing.py (constant amplitude stream yields near-zero variance/motion; injected periodic perturbations raise motion_score; outlier spike is suppressed by Hampel; quality flags insufficient for low packet rate and stale data; CSI length change resets cleanly), tests/test_activity.py (threshold mapping incl. unknown on bad quality), tests/test_engine.py (Engine with ReplaySource on the fixture processes packets and snapshot has counters), tests/test_dashboard.py using streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest.from_file('dashboard/app.py') running without exceptions. Test signals may be generated in-test as plain numpy arrays (unit tests only, not presented as data).
Update README.md with Milestone 2 usage (make dashboard, choosing port, replay) and what each panel means.
acceptance_criteria: make test passes including new processing, activity, engine and AppTest dashboard tests
Streamlit app starts headless and /_stcore/health returns ok
Replaying tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt through the dashboard engine produces a non-empty heatmap matrix and motion frames (verified via Engine test)
With no data source connected the dashboard shows 'no data' states rather than any numbers
Dark theme config present and Streamlit usage stats disabled
verification: .venv/bin/streamlit run dashboard/app.py --server.headless true --server.port 8599 (in background), then curl -s http://localhost:8599/_stcore/health, then stop the server
